newsitem.title: THAILAND: Extra-territorial laws urged against child sex.
newsitem.headline: Extra-territorial laws urged against child sex.

text.p: Child rights activists on Tuesday urged countries to adopt extra-territorial laws to stamp out child prostitution.

Despite progress at the first World Congress Against Commercial Sexual Exploitation of Children in Stockholm last year, eradication of child prostitution faces many hurdles, said Vitit Muntarbhorn, director of Child Rights Asianet and rapporteur general of the Stockholm congress.

He told the annual meeting of the international child rights organisation ECPAT some governments were reluctant to adopt extra-territorial laws to prosecute their nationals who buy child sex in other countries.

ECPAT -- originally End Child Prostitution in Asian Tourism -- was expanded after the Stockholm conference. While keeping the acronym ECPAT, it widened its brief to cover the world and changed its name to End Child Prostitution, Child Pronography and the Trafficking of Children for Sexual Purposes.
Thailand planned to eradicate the commercial sexual exploitation of children, said Wanchai Roujanavong of the country's Attorney-General's office.
About 25 percent of Thailand's 200,000 prostitutes were less than 18 years old, Wanchai said.
Last year a tough new child prostitution prevention law went into effect in Thailand. It increased the penalties for sex with children to a maximum 20 years from a maximum three months.
